questions.scenario: A logistics company sends each bill of lading to Claude Haiku 5.5 with a single tool, `record_shipment`, and the default `tool_choice`. The system prompt says 'Always call record_shipment.' The worker reads the first `tool_use` block of each response. In production, 5% of responses contain only text, such as 'Here are the shipment details I found: …', with `stop_reason: "end_turn"`, and the worker silently drops those documents. The team has already set `strict: true` on the tool. What is the most effective fix?
options: Strengthen the system prompt to 'You MUST call record_shipment and never answer in plain text', and repeat it in the user turn.
Set tool_choice to {"type": "tool", "name": "record_shipment"}, so every response is required to call that tool.
Keep the defaults and, when a response has no tool_use block, parse the text reply with a regex to recover the fields.
Add input_examples to record_shipment, so the model sees concrete calls and becomes more inclined to use the tool.
questions.why_correct: Con el `tool_choice` por defecto (`auto`), Claude decide en cada turno si llamar una tool o contestar. El prompt orienta esa decisión pero no la garantiza. Para exigir la llamada, la doc dice: usá `tool_choice`. Haiku 5.5 acepta forced tool use, y `strict` ya cubre la validez de los inputs.

why_wrong.0: Más fuerte sigue siendo guía: baja el 5% pero no lo lleva a cero.
why_wrong.2: Parsear texto con regex es la señal de que eso tendría que haber sido una tool call. Es frágil y trata el síntoma.
why_wrong.3: Los ejemplos mejoran CÓMO se llama la tool, no garantizan QUE se llame.

questions.rule: Prompt orienta, `tool_choice` garantiza. Si el downstream necesita SIEMPRE la tool call, forzala (en modelos que lo soportan).
questions.source_quote: To require a tool call rather than rely on prompting, set tool_choice.

questions.scenario: An accounts-payable pipeline on Claude Haiku 5.5 receives three document types that it cannot tell apart in advance: invoices, receipts and credit notes. Each type has its own strict extraction tool: `extract_invoice`, `extract_receipt` and `extract_credit_note`. Today `tool_choice` is `{"type": "tool", "name": "extract_invoice"}` because invoices are 70% of volume. Receipts and credit notes now come back as invoices with empty or invented fields, and 9% of credit notes were paid instead of credited. When the team briefly tried `auto`, some responses were plain text. What configuration should they use?
options: Keep forcing extract_invoice, but add optional receipt and credit-note fields to it so one tool can represent all three types.
Use tool_choice auto with a system prompt instruction to always call exactly one of the three extraction tools.
Use tool_choice {"type": "any"} with the three strict tools, so Claude must call one of them and chooses which one.
Classify the document type in a first call with a text answer, then force the matching tool by name in a second call.
questions.why_correct: `any` obliga a usar una de las tools disponibles sin forzar cuál: Claude elige la que corresponde al documento. Combinado con `strict: true`, la doc dice que garantizás las dos cosas: que se llama una de tus tools y que los inputs cumplen el schema. Es la configuración para varios schemas de extracción posibles.

why_wrong.0: Una tool frankenstein con campos opcionales de tres tipos invita a mezclar y a inventar, y el forzado sigue eligiendo por vos.
why_wrong.1: Ya vieron que `auto` a veces responde texto: la instrucción orienta, no garantiza.
why_wrong.3: Casi: funciona, pero agrega una llamada y parsea una clasificación en texto libre, cuando `any` resuelve la elección en una sola llamada con garantía.

questions.rule: Varias tools de extracción y no sabés cuál aplica → `tool_choice: any` + `strict`. `tool` es para cuando sabés cuál.
questions.source_quote: On models that support forced tool use, combine tool_choice: {"type": "any"} with strict tool use to guarantee both that one of your tools is called and that the tool inputs strictly follow your schema.

questions.scenario: A bank's support agent runs on Claude Haiku 5.5 with `tool_choice: {"type": "any"}` and strict tools for `lookup_account`, `freeze_card` and `escalate_to_human`, so every turn produces a tool call. To improve answers on complex disputes, the team switches the model ID to `claude-opus-5-5` without any other change. Every request now fails with a 400 `invalid_request_error`: `tool_choice: type "tool" and "any" are not supported for this model.` The model change has been approved and cannot be reverted. What is the correct change?
options: Switch to tool_choice auto, keep strict: true on the tools, and handle turns where the model replies in text instead.
Switch to tool_choice {"type": "tool"} with the most common tool name, since only the any option is rejected here.
Keep tool_choice any and disable thinking on the request, since forced tool use is only rejected while thinking is on.
Keep tool_choice any and send these requests through the Message Batches API, which accepts forced tool use on any model.
questions.why_correct: Opus 5.5 no soporta forced tool use: `any` y `tool` devuelven 400, sin importar la config de thinking. Lo que sí acepta es `auto` (y `none`). La doc indica `auto` con strict tool use para mantener los inputs válidos, y tu código tiene que manejar el turno en que el modelo contesta en texto.

why_wrong.1: El mensaje de error dice explícitamente que ni `tool` ni `any` están soportados en este modelo.
why_wrong.2: En estos modelos el rechazo es por modelo, "regardless of thinking settings". Apagar thinking no cambia nada.
why_wrong.3: Batches procesa los mismos parámetros de la Messages API: el modelo sigue sin aceptar forced tool use.

questions.rule: Opus 5.5 / Sonnet 5.5: no hay forced tool use. Usá `auto` + `strict` (o structured outputs si querés la respuesta en JSON).
questions.source_quote: Claude Fable 5.2, Claude Mythos 5.2, Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Sonnet 5.5, Claude Fable 5.1, and Claude Mythos 5.1 don’t support forced tool use.

questions.scenario: A research coordinator on Claude Haiku 5.5, with adaptive thinking on by default, asks a synthesis subagent to weigh conflicting sources and then call `submit_findings`. To guarantee the call, the team set `tool_choice: {"type": "tool", "name": "submit_findings"}`. Since that change, the share of findings that ignore contradicting sources rose from 6% to 19%, and responses no longer contain any thinking block. The team wants the model to reason about conflicts before submitting, and it can tolerate handling an occasional text-only reply. What should they change?
options: Keep forcing submit_findings and add a reasoning string field to its schema where the model explains its weighting in steps.
Keep forcing the tool and switch to manual extended thinking with a budget_tokens value, so the model must think first.
Keep forcing the tool and ask in the system prompt that the model think carefully about conflicting sources before calling it.
Use tool_choice auto with an instruction to call submit_findings, so the model can think before it makes the tool call.
questions.why_correct: Forzar una tool saltea el thinking: la respuesta arranca directo con el bloque `tool_use`. Por eso cayó la calidad. La doc dice que para dejar pensar al modelo antes de la llamada, uses `auto` con una instrucción en el prompt. El equipo acepta manejar algún turno en texto, así que es el trade-off correcto.

why_wrong.0: Un campo de razonamiento dentro del schema no recupera el thinking, y la doc advierte que pedir razonamiento paso a paso como propiedad puede terminar en un refusal.
why_wrong.1: Thinking manual (`thinking: {type: "enabled"}`) con `any` o `tool` no está soportado y da error.
why_wrong.2: Con la tool forzada no hay bloque de thinking: la instrucción no tiene dónde ejecutarse.

questions.rule: Forced tool use = sin thinking. ¿Necesitás que razone antes? `auto` + instrucción, y manejá el caso de texto.
questions.source_quote: Forcing a tool also skips thinking on every model that accepts forced tool use: the response starts with the tool_use block and has no thinking block. To let the model think before it calls the tool, use auto with a prompt instruction in the same way.

questions.scenario: A CI step uses Claude Sonnet 5.5 with `tool_choice: auto` and a strict tool, `report_findings`, to collect review results. The script does `block = response.content[0]` and reads `block.input`. On about 12% of runs it crashes with `AttributeError: 'TextBlock' object has no attribute 'input'`. In those responses the first block is a sentence like 'I'll record the findings now.', followed by a `tool_use` block, and `stop_reason` is `tool_use`. Forced tool use is not available on this model. What is the right fix?
options: Add 'Do not write any text before calling report_findings' to the system prompt, so the tool_use block always comes first.
Iterate over response.content and read the input of the block whose type is tool_use, instead of assuming it comes first.
Retry the request whenever content[0] is a text block, up to three times, until the tool_use block comes back first.
Read response.content[-1] instead, because with auto the tool_use block is always the last block of the response.
questions.why_correct: Con `auto`, Claude muchas veces comenta lo que va a hacer antes de llamar la tool. La respuesta trae `stop_reason: "tool_use"` y uno o más bloques `tool_use` que pueden no ser el primero. El código tiene que recorrer `content` y tomar los bloques de tipo `tool_use`, sin depender de la posición ni del texto.

why_wrong.0: Es guía: baja el porcentaje pero el código sigue rompiendo cuando el modelo comenta igual.
why_wrong.2: Paga llamadas extra para esquivar un bug de parsing que se arregla en el código.
why_wrong.3: Casi: suele andar, pero no está garantizado (puede haber varios bloques `tool_use` o texto después). Sigue dependiendo de la posición.

questions.rule: Nunca asumas `content[0]`: recorré los bloques y filtrá por `type == "tool_use"`.
questions.source_quote: When using tools, Claude often comments on what it’s doing or responds naturally to the user before calling tools.

questions.scenario: A company gates merges with a CI job that calls Claude Sonnet 5.5 through the API and expects a verdict object, `{"decision": "approve" | "block", "reasons": [...]}`. Today the job defines a tool, `submit_verdict`, with `strict: true`, uses `tool_choice: auto`, and has the system prompt 'Always call submit_verdict.' On about 2% of PRs the model answers in prose and the gate fails open, letting unreviewed code merge. Sonnet 5.5 is mandated by the security team. Nothing in this job calls an external function: the verdict is the whole output. What is the most reliable fix?
options: Set tool_choice to {"type": "tool", "name": "submit_verdict"}, so every response is guaranteed to be a submit_verdict call.
Keep auto with the strict tool, and make the gate fail closed by blocking the merge whenever a response has no tool_use block.
Drop the tool and put the verdict schema in output_config.format, so the response itself is constrained to that JSON shape.
Keep auto with the strict tool and reinforce the system prompt with an example conversation that ends in a submit_verdict call.
questions.why_correct: En Sonnet 5.5 no hay forced tool use, y con `auto` la llamada no está garantizada. Pero acá no hace falta ninguna función: lo que se necesita es que la respuesta tenga una forma JSON fija. Para eso la doc indica structured outputs (`output_config.format`): cada respuesta sale con el veredicto válido.

why_wrong.1: Casi: fallar cerrado es buena higiene de seguridad, pero no arregla nada: el 2% de PRs queda bloqueado sin veredicto y hay que re-correrlos.
why_wrong.3: Un ejemplo más es guía: baja el 2% pero no da garantía.

questions.rule: ¿La salida ES el dato y no hay función que llamar? → structured outputs, no una tool que esperás que se llame.
questions.source_quote: auto with strict tool use to guarantee schema-valid tool inputs, or structured outputs when you need a response in a fixed JSON shape.

questions.scenario: A contract-analysis service runs on Claude Haiku 5.5 with `tool_choice: {"type": "any"}` and three strict extraction tools. Analysts asked for deeper reasoning on indemnity clauses, so a developer added `thinking: {"type": "enabled", "budget_tokens": 6000}` to the requests. Every request now fails with an error. For the downstream system, a guaranteed call to one of the three tools is non-negotiable; extra reasoning would be nice to have but is optional. The developer believes thinking and forced tool use simply cannot be combined on any model. Which change should the team make?
options: Remove the manual thinking parameter and keep tool_choice any; adaptive thinking does not block forced tool use, though a forced call skips thinking.
Keep manual thinking and switch to tool_choice {"type": "tool"} for the most common tool, which manual thinking does accept.
Keep manual thinking and lower budget_tokens below max_tokens, because the error comes from the budget exceeding the response limit.
Keep manual thinking and tool_choice any, but move these requests to Claude Sonnet 5.5, which supports both features together.
questions.why_correct: El error lo causa el thinking manual (`thinking: {type: "enabled"}`): con él, `any` y `tool` no están soportados. El thinking adaptativo, que Haiku 5.5 trae por defecto, no bloquea el forced tool use; la llamada forzada simplemente saltea el thinking. Sacando el parámetro manual recuperás la garantía, que es lo innegociable.

why_wrong.1: Con thinking manual tampoco se acepta `tool`: el error es para `any` y `tool` por igual.
why_wrong.2: No es un problema de presupuesto: es una incompatibilidad documentada entre thinking manual y forced tool use.
why_wrong.3: Sonnet 5.5 no soporta forced tool use con ninguna configuración de thinking: empeora.

questions.rule: Thinking manual + `any`/`tool` = error. Thinking adaptativo sí convive con forced tool use (pero la llamada forzada no piensa).
questions.source_quote: Adaptive thinking itself doesn’t block forced tool use (models with thinking on by default, such as Claude Opus 5 and Claude Haiku 5.5, accept it, but a forced call skips thinking: the response starts with the tool call and has no thinking block)

questions.scenario: A telecom's support agent on Claude Haiku 5.5 handles long conversations, often 40 or more turns, with prompt caching on the system prompt, tool definitions and conversation history. A new orchestration layer sets `tool_choice` to `{"type": "tool", "name": "verify_identity"}` on the first turn of each sensitive request, switches back to `auto` on the next turn, and forces `escalate_to_human` whenever a frustration score crosses a threshold. Since that change, cache-read tokens on long conversations dropped 55% and cost per conversation rose 30%, although the system prompt and tools never change. What explains this, and what should the team do?
options: Tool definitions are re-tokenized whenever tool_choice changes; move the tools into the system prompt as text so they stay cached.
Forced tool use turns off prompt caching for the whole request; replace forcing with stronger prompt instructions on those turns.
Cache entries expire faster on forced turns; switch the cache to a longer TTL so the entries survive between conversation turns.
Changing tool_choice invalidates cached message blocks (tools and system stay cached); keep tool_choice stable across turns.
questions.why_correct: La doc lo dice: cambiar `tool_choice` invalida los bloques de mensajes cacheados. Las definiciones de tools y el system prompt siguen en cache, pero el historial se reprocesa. En conversaciones de 40 turnos el historial es casi todo el input, así que cada cambio de `tool_choice` es caro. Hay que minimizar esos cambios.

why_wrong.0: Al revés: tools y system prompt siguen cacheados. Pasar las tools a texto rompe el tool use sin resolver nada.
why_wrong.1: Forzar no apaga el caching: lo que se invalida son los bloques de mensajes por el CAMBIO de `tool_choice`. Y pasar a instrucciones pierde la garantía.
why_wrong.2: No es un tema de TTL: la invalidación pasa por el cambio del parámetro, no por el paso del tiempo.

questions.rule: Cambiar `tool_choice` entre turnos invalida el cache del historial (no el de tools/system). Mantenelo estable.
questions.source_quote: When using prompt caching, changes to the tool_choice parameter will invalidate cached message blocks. Tool definitions and system prompts remain cached, but message content must be reprocessed.

questions.scenario: A research assistant on Claude Haiku 5.5 runs an agentic loop with the tools `web_search` and `fetch_page`. After the loop, the orchestrator sends one last request asking for a final prose briefing for the user, keeping the same tool definitions and history so the conversation stays valid. In 14% of runs that final request returns another `web_search` call instead of the briefing, and the orchestrator, which has no budget left for more searches, returns an empty briefing. Prompt wording such as 'Do not search anymore, write the briefing now' helped but did not stop it. What is the most reliable change for the final request?
options: Set tool_choice to {"type": "auto"} explicitly on the final request, since auto lets the model choose to answer directly.
Set tool_choice to {"type": "none"} on the final request, which prevents Claude from using any of the provided tools.
Lower max_tokens on the final request, so the model has no room to plan another search and has to write the briefing.
Set tool_choice to {"type": "any"} and add a write_briefing tool whose input is the final prose, then render that input.
questions.why_correct: `tool_choice` también sirve para el caso inverso: `none` impide que Claude use cualquiera de las tools. Mantenés las definiciones y el historial, y la respuesta final es texto sí o sí. Es enforcement, no una sugerencia en el prompt.

why_wrong.0: `auto` es lo que ya tienen (es el default con tools): deja que el modelo elija buscar otra vez.
why_wrong.2: Bajar `max_tokens` no impide una tool call (son pocos tokens) y puede cortar el briefing a la mitad.
why_wrong.3: Casi: `any` obliga a usar alguna tool, pero no cuál. `web_search` sigue siendo una opción válida.

questions.rule: ¿Necesitás que NO llame tools en un paso? → `tool_choice: none`. Garantiza texto, sin sacar las tools del request.
questions.source_quote: none prevents Claude from using any tools. This is the default value when no tools are provided.

questions.scenario: A mortgage lender's intake pipeline on Claude Haiku 5.5 forces a strict tool, `extract_application`, with `tool_choice: {"type": "tool", "name": "extract_application"}` for every uploaded file. About 7% of uploads are not loan applications at all: pay stubs, marketing flyers, blank scans. For those, the model still calls `extract_application` with schema-valid but meaningless data, and underwriters waste hours on phantom applications. Compliance requires that every rejected file be logged with a reason, and the pipeline must keep a guaranteed structured result for every file. What is the most effective change?
options: Keep forcing extract_application and add a required boolean is_loan_application field, so non-applications get flagged in the same call.
Switch to tool_choice auto and let the model answer in plain text when the file is not a loan application, then skip those files.
Add a strict reject_document tool with a reason enum, and use tool_choice {"type": "any"} so Claude must call one of the two tools.
Add a pre-filter call that classifies each upload with a text answer, and only send the files labeled 'application' to the extractor.
questions.why_correct: Forzar una sola tool obliga a tratar todo como solicitud. Con `any`, Claude tiene que usar una de las tools disponibles pero elige cuál: `extract_application` para las solicitudes, `reject_document` para el resto. Sigue habiendo un resultado estructurado garantizado por archivo, y sin datos fantasma.

why_wrong.0: Casi: marca el caso, pero el schema forzado sigue obligando a llenar todos los campos requeridos de la solicitud con datos inventados.
why_wrong.1: Pierde la garantía de resultado estructurado que pide la restricción: con `auto` el texto puede aparecer también en solicitudes reales.
why_wrong.3: Suma una llamada y depende de parsear texto libre, cuando una segunda tool + `any` resuelve las dos cosas en una.

questions.rule: Si "ninguna de las anteriores" es una respuesta válida, dale una tool para eso y usá `any`, no fuerces una sola tool.
questions.source_quote: any tells Claude that it must use one of the provided tools, but doesn’t force a particular tool.
